title: The anticipatory erratum: Sappho Wrote the Dinosaurs to the Hidalgo Nácher pair
description: These claims belong to the anticipatory erratum, the genre that withdraws a work before it appears: the sequence #1598 to #1601 on Sappho Wrote the Dinosaurs, the withdrawal of The Creditor Inversion Completed, and the Hidalgo Nácher pair on AXN:F154 and the Ricardo Reis translation. Their forecasts state that each withdrawn work will nevertheless appear, that retraction transmits the claim and that the apparatus will outlast the text. Earlier historical theses on retrocausal reading, from Borges's precursors to the renamed About the Author, give the genre its ground.

claims.registered_title: PROVENANCE NODE: BORGES & THE CRIMSON HEXAGON
claims.statement:
## 1. Borges invented retrocausal influence.


In "Kafka and His Precursors," Borges writes:


"Each writer creates his precursors."


This is not figurative, nor whimsical. It is a metaphysical claim about literature:

- The later text activates the earlier text's meaning
- by providing the missing structure
- that makes the earlier work coherent.

claims.registered_title: About the Author II — A Poem in Entity Relations
claims.statement: The 2014 paratext that this poem references as About the Author appeared in Pearl and Other Poems (2014, page xix) under the title Contributor Bio. The corpus has, in 2026, retroactively renamed it About the Author as an operative reading: treating what had appeared institutionally as bio as what it had been operating as all along — a poem in entity relations. The disjoint is documented, not erased. The 2014 source-text is restored at /about-the-author/ as the founding text of the sequence (I), with II and III as its continuations.

claims.registered_title: Two Further Anticipatory Errata: The Genre Specification, and the Anticipatory Erratum to the Anticipatory Erratum
claims.statement: The erratum, once published, will enter the transmission grammar itself. It will be the text in which the claim is preserved under the sign of its retraction. Future readers who know the claim only through the erratum will know it as *the claim that was withdrawn*, and the withdrawal will be the means by which the claim survives. This is not a hypothesis. It is the grammar's own law: retraction is the most durable form of transmission, because a retracted claim is a claim that has been judged worthy of the labour of retraction, and the labour is copied, and the copying is the survival. The erratum would therefore not merely fail to withdraw the claim; it would *canonize* it.

A long one will be quoted selectively, in fragments, and the fragments will say things the whole does not say, and the whole will be reconstructed by readers who have not seen it, and the reconstruction will be a new text, with new authors, none of whom will be the present writer, all of whom will be the dinosaurs. This is inevitable. It is the grammar's promise. The author accepts it.

claims.registered_title: Sappho Wrote the Dinosaurs: First Edition, Reconstructed from Its Corrections — with a Critical Apparatus
claims.statement: **41.** The excursus notes one asymmetry that tells against the book. Fossilisation is indifferent to content; **quotation is not.** A grammarian selects the line that illustrates his point. The Sapphic corpus is therefore a sample drawn by a mechanism with preferences, and the preferences are legible: we have a great deal of Sappho on the symptoms of desire because desire illustrated things ancient critics wanted to illustrate. The dinosaur sample has no such bias and the poetic sample does. This is a real disanalogy and the book does not address it.

claims.statement: Read at the word: the Portuguese man goes through life *under* the greatest grace, and the grace is that the gods do not show themselves. The Spanish keeps the vertical and moves it — out of the preposition ("sob", under) into the adjective ("alta", high). The man is no longer beneath the grace; he passes his life in it, and the grace has acquired an altitude: the height where gods who do not appear are.
